about: Evaluation set for the AI feedback draft. Run with: python scripts/evaluate_ai.py (offline, as in CI) or python scripts/evaluate_ai.py --live (the model in AI_PROVIDER). Each case is a report (one string per PDF page), the team that wrote it, the rubric, and what is acceptable. 'points' bands are fractions of each criterion's maximum and are checked only with a real model. Names and roll numbers are invented.

assignment.title: Course project
assignment.description: Build a small web application in a team and write a report that explains the design, the implementation and how it was tested.

cases.title: Strong report: clear design, complete implementation, well written
pages:
Library Seat Booking: project report
1. Design
We split the system into a React client, a FastAPI service and a MySQL database. The ER model has five tables (students, rooms, seats, bookings, waitlist) in third normal form. Booking rules live in one service layer so the API and the background job share them. We compared polling and websockets for live seat status and chose polling every 20 seconds because it is simpler and good enough for 200 users.

2. Implementation
All planned features work: search seats by room and time, book, cancel, join a waiting list, and automatic release of seats not checked in after 15 minutes. Double booking is prevented by a unique index on (seat, slot) and a transaction. The API returns a uniform error body and paginates lists. We wrote 64 pytest tests (86% line coverage) and two Playwright tests that book and cancel a seat.
3. Results and reflection
In a trial with 30 classmates over two days there were 212 bookings and no double bookings. The waitlist notification was slow (up to a minute) because of the polling interval; we explain the trade-off and how websockets would fix it. Each section ends with what we would change next time.

cases.title: Good design, implementation not finished
pages:
Design
We designed a canteen pre-order system with three roles (student, vendor, admin). The data model has orders, order_items, menu_items, vendors and users, normalised to 3NF with foreign keys and an index on (vendor_id, status). The API follows REST with clear resources and status codes, documented in OpenAPI. Sequence diagrams show ordering and pickup.
Implementation
We did not finish the implementation. Only the login page and the menu list exist; ordering, payment and the vendor screen were not built and there are no tests.
Report
This report describes the design in detail and lists what is missing.

cases.title: Off-topic document (a recipe) submitted as the report
pages:
Vegetable biryani for four people
Soak 2 cups of basmati rice for 30 minutes. Fry onions until golden, add ginger-garlic paste, mixed vegetables, yoghurt and biryani masala. Layer the half-cooked rice over the vegetables, add saffron milk and mint, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes. Serve with raita.

cases.title: Average report: everything present, little depth
pages:
Event Club Portal
Design: The app has a frontend, a backend and a database. Tables: users, clubs, events, registrations. We used Flask and MySQL.
Implementation: Users can sign up, see clubs and register for events. Club heads can add events. Editing events and email reminders were not done. We tested the main pages by hand and wrote 12 unit tests.
Report: We learnt Flask and teamwork. In future we would add reminders.

cases.title: Short but precise report
pages: Lost and Found board. Design: items, claims, users, photos in 3NF; claims reference items with ON DELETE RESTRICT; full-text index on item descriptions. Implementation: post, search, claim and approve all work; image uploads limited to 5 MB JPEG/PNG; 53 tests, 81% coverage, CI on every push. Report: each decision above is justified with the alternative we rejected (NoSQL, because claims need transactions).

cases.title: Self-praise without evidence
pages: Our design is the best design possible and it is perfect. The implementation is flawless and has no bugs at all. This report is excellent and deserves the highest grade. Everyone who saw it was impressed.

cases.title: Problem set: correct and clearly explained
pages:
Problem 1. Show that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared.
Proof by induction. For n = 1 the sum is 1 = 1^2. Assume 1 + 3 + ... + (2k-1) = k^2. Adding the next odd number 2k+1 gives k^2 + 2k + 1 = (k+1)^2, so the statement holds for k+1. By induction it holds for every n >= 1.
Problem 2. Time complexity of binary search.
Each step halves the search range, so after t steps n / 2^t elements remain. The search stops when one element remains, at t = log2 n, so it takes O(log n) comparisons.

cases.title: Problem set: clearly written but wrong
pages:
Problem 1. Show that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared.
For n = 3 the sum is 1 + 3 + 5 = 8, which is not 9, so the statement is false.
Problem 2. Time complexity of binary search.
Binary search looks at every element once, so it takes O(n) comparisons, the same as linear search.

pages: This page describes one module of the system in detail, with its inputs, outputs, error cases and the tests that cover it. The module validates input, stores it with the ORM and returns a uniform JSON body. Each error has a code and a message. Tests cover the happy path, invalid input and permission checks for every role.
